common.collapseNavHint: Collapse the menu — it will open on hover

setup.title: First run
setup.subtitle: Create the administrator account. The password is stored on your server and nowhere else.
setup.glossHint: Russian dictionary data is markedly thinner than English. If you choose Russian, missing senses fall back to English and are labelled as a fallback rather than substituted silently.
setup.passwordHint: At least {min} characters. Length matters more than special characters.

local.title: This machine
local.subtitle: What is already installed here, and the two things you can add later.

ready.vocabulary: The starter language pack: frequent vocabulary with its forms, translations and real examples — sentences written by native speakers, not by us.
ready.course: The six-month course and the grammar curriculum underneath it.
ready.audio: Recorded audio for the ear trainer's minimal pairs.

local.readyHint: All of it came inside the binary and installed itself on first boot. Nothing to download, nothing to configure — you can start learning as soon as this wizard closes.
local.noPack: The starter pack did not install. The app will still run, but every language feature stays dead until a pack is present in the data directory — the server log says why.
local.extrasHint: Both are set to “later”, deliberately. A modest machine should not be pushed through a 252 MB download before its owner has read a word of Hungarian.
local.fullPackLater: Later — the starter pack is enough to begin
local.fullPackHint: 252 MB: much wider vocabulary and far more sentences to collect from. It changes how much material there is, not what the app does with it.
local.fullPackBuildHint: It is built from source rather than downloaded. In a clone of the repository, run:
local.speechLater: Later — the app is complete without them
local.speechNow: Take me to their settings after this
local.speechHint: Optional sidecars. Without them there is no synthesised audio and no pronunciation feedback; everything else behaves exactly the same.
local.laterInSettings: Both of these live in Settings afterwards, and the About section there reports which pack is actually installed.

today.title: Today

loopHints.memory: Spaced review. In the morning, before email.
loopHints.input: Comprehensible audio or text. Commuting, exercising, cooking.
loopHints.study: Grammar on odd days, collecting sentences from your own texts on even ones.
loopHints.human: A live teacher or tandem partner. Twice a week.

today.humanNotice: The app cannot tick this off for you. A real person is the one irreplaceable part: a model has no social stakes, understands your broken Hungarian far too well, and will tell you nothing about your pauses or intonation.

empty.title: Ready to start
empty.body: The language pack is not installed yet, so all four loops are empty. The app runs; the material arrives with the pack.

today.streakHint: A day counts when the due queue is cleared and your stated minutes are met — not when the app was opened.

streak.title: Streak: {n} days
streak.rule: A day counts when the queue is clear AND the minutes are met — both.
streak.noFreeze: There are no freezes and no paid repairs here: the streak shows obligations met, not obligations bought. A missed day is simply missed.

plan.title: Plan
plan.aheadNotice: This one sits further down the plan. Nothing stops you taking it now — the order is advice and the app does not enforce it.
plan.orderNotice: “Ahead” is not “locked”. A unit counts as done when every one of its words is in your review deck, and you may start anywhere you like.

word.partialNotice: Some of these are already in your deck, but the plan reports a count rather than naming them — so they are left unmarked instead of guessed at. Take the unit on and the list becomes exact.
word.noMaterialNotice: The language pack has no sentence for these words, and a card here is a sentence. We will not invent one: it would be Hungarian nobody has written. They stay part of the unit, and the full language pack may well have examples for them.

plan.enrolHint: Every word becomes a card built from a real sentence containing it — never a bare word pair, which would teach nothing about the morphology carrying the meaning.

report.duplicate: Already in your deck, so not duplicated: {n}.
report.skippedWhy: A card here is a sentence with a real example, and the language pack has no example for these words. We will not invent one: it would be Hungarian nobody has written. The translation stays with you and the words stay part of the unit — the full language pack may well have examples for them.
report.none: Nothing new to add: every word of this unit is already in your deck.

plan.browseResources: Where to read on your own
plan.noCourse: The course ships inside the language pack. A pack built before the course existed serves everything else and leaves this screen empty.

handOver.title: The prescribed course ends here
handOver.done: Every unit of the course is done — all {n} of them — and every word in them is in your review deck.
handOver.why: The app stops prescribing vocabulary on purpose. What carries you from here is volume of reading and listening, and it has to be material you chose: a course that never ends produces a learner who can only read what was made for them.
handOver.next: The machinery stays. The review deck, sentence collection, the grammar drills and the ear trainer all keep working exactly as before — what changes is where the material comes from.

plan.fromElsewhere: {n} of these were already in the deck — from reading or another unit

resources.title: Where to go next
resources.intro: Places to find your own Hungarian, now that the course has stopped handing it to you. Each entry names the level it becomes usable at — the point where it stops being decoding, not the level it is written at.
resources.empty: This language pack carries no catalogue. The list ships with the pack rather than with the app, so a newer pack will bring one — nothing here is broken.

settings.title: Settings

review.desiredRetentionHint: The share of cards you should recall. Below 0.80 material decays before it consolidates; above 0.95 workload grows faster than the benefit.
review.newPerDayHint: The most common reason people abandon spaced repetition is the review avalanche three weeks in. This limit is what prevents it.
review.goalHint: Your goal reweights the card directions: you get back what you train.
review.accentToleranceHint: Type viszlat for viszlát and the answer counts, rated Hard, with the missing mark underlined: hat and hát are different words, and vowel length stays something to learn. The spelling direction is exempt — it exists precisely for the diacritics.

drill.title: Grammar drills
drill.gateHint: Topics are drilled in blocks until accuracy reaches this threshold, and only then interleaved. Interleaving too early prevents the rule from consolidating — this contradicts the common advice, deliberately.

services.hint: All optional, and the core of the app works with every one of them stopped. Speech comes from your own device by default and needs no configuration — the other three matter only if you are running the corresponding service yourself.

settings.clamped: “{field}” was pulled back into range: {from} became {to}.

curriculum.title: Exam
curriculum.examHint: A pre-booked, pre-paid exam is the best-known defence against the month-4–7 motivational trough. The Today screen counts down to it.

sound.title: Feedback sounds
sound.hint: A short tone on every answer, and one when something real is finished. Synthesised in the browser — nothing is downloaded and nothing is scored.
sound.preview: Switching it on plays the tone.

edition.starter: starter — the one inside the binary

language.glossFallback: Fall back to the other language when a meaning is missing
language.glossFallbackHint: The pack has 8,620 Russian glosses against 45,917 English ones. With this on you see the English meaning marked as a substitute rather than an empty card; with it off, a word with no meaning in your language shows none.

hvpt.title: Ear trainer
hvpt.hint: How many distinct voices a session needs before it will run, and how many trials it contains.
hvpt.floorCaveat: The research asks for five or more voices: talker variability is the active ingredient, and it is what transfers the skill to real speech. The current language pack ships three, so a floor of 5 means no session will ever start. You can lower the floor, but some of the effect goes with it, and the app will not pretend otherwise.

mt.title: Local translator
mt.notRunning: The service is not answering. Most likely the container is not up — one command on the server, and everything after that is here:
mt.downloading: Downloading the model. This happens once.
mt.hint: The model lives inside the service and weighs about 2.4 GB. The app cannot start a container that was never deployed — but everything after that is set from here. Switch the translator off above and its buttons disappear across the app.

data.hint: Your whole profile in one file: both spaced-repetition state spaces, the review log, words, texts, analyses and tutor chats. To move it to your own server — or just to keep a copy.
data.exportHint: You get a .zip: profile.json with every table, and a media folder with your materials' audio.
data.secrets: Service API keys are not in the file and do not travel — enter them again on the new install. They are left out precisely because the file leaves the server.
data.importHint: Replaces the current profile with the file's contents. Other accounts on this server are untouched.
data.confirmBody: This is not a merge. Everything in your profile right now is erased and replaced by the file's contents. There is no undo. You currently have:
data.confirmBlocking: The import runs as one transaction: the app does not respond until it finishes. If anything goes wrong, exactly what you had is what remains.

report.title: Rows imported: {rows}
report.replay: The review log was verified: {n} cards were replayed from scratch and matched the state that arrived with them. No interchange format could make that check.
report.skipped: The file carries fields this version has no home for: {cols}. They were not imported — said plainly rather than swallowed.
report.reloading: The page is about to reload: everything on screen belongs to the old profile.

settings.adminOnly: Only an administrator can change these settings.

users.title: Accounts
users.listHint: Everyone signs in separately and keeps their own cards, texts and progress. Settings are shared, so only an administrator can change them.
users.addHint: They sign in with this address and password, and can change the password themselves afterwards.

password.title: Change your password
password.hint: This signs you out on every other device, but not here.
password.mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.

capabilities.groupLabel: Status of the optional services (speech, recognition, analysis, model, translation) — not your progress.

errors.network-unreachable: The server is not answering. Check that it is running.
errors.notFoundBody: There is no such page here.
errors.llmOff: No language model is configured. Connect one in Settings → Services → LLM.
errors.llmFailed: The model did not answer usefully. The level estimate was left as it was.
errors.levelManual: The level was set by hand — the model does not overwrite it.
errors.tutorBusy: One question at a time — the tutor is still answering the previous one.
errors.tutorCorpus: The tutor's reference corpus did not load. The server log says why.
errors.tutorFailed: The model did not answer usefully. Nothing was changed.
errors.llmNoModel: No model is chosen. Name one in Settings → Services → Language model — the endpoint's own list is offered there.
errors.tutorNoMessage: That question is no longer in the chat.
errors.tutorNoCard: No such card — the word may have been set aside.
errors.tutorNoThread: There is no such chat — it may have been deleted.
errors.server: The server answered with an error; the details are in its log.
errors.sessionExpired: Your session ended — sign in again.
errors.emailTaken: That email address is already in use.
errors.wrongPassword: The current password is not right.
errors.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts — wait a moment.
errors.trialExpired: This trial has expired — start a new session.
errors.gone: That is gone — it may have been removed.
errors.known: This word is marked known — it is no longer asked.

tutor.hint: Ask the AI tutor about this card — it does not affect the word's schedule
tutor.title: Tutor · this card
tutor.beforeAnswer: Before you answer the tutor is not given the answer and will not name it. Asking changes nothing about the word's schedule: the card still asks you, and the grade is yours.

chips.hintRule: Which form is needed, and why? (hint)

review.allDoneBody: The queue is empty and nothing returns today. Come back tomorrow — spacing only works if you keep to it.
review.newCapped: New cards still waiting: {n}. The daily limit is reached — that is a guard, not a fault: it is what stops the review avalanche three weeks from now.
review.keysInspect: click a word for its breakdown
review.paceDone: That's the new material for today
review.paceDoneBody: Everything due has been reviewed and today's ration of new words is used up. The rest is queued — that is the design.
review.paceWaiting: Waiting their turn: {words} new words ({cards} new cards in total — each word has several directions: recognise, produce, fill the gap).
review.paceDays: Started today: {today} of {perDay} cards. At this pace the queue clears in about {days} days.
review.paceWhy: The limit is a guard, not a fault. Every new word comes back for review again and again; taking a hundred today means a queue three weeks from now that cannot be cleared. That is how people quit.
review.acceptedAccents: Accepted without diacritics. The full spelling is “{expected}”: vowel length changes meaning in Hungarian.

directionHint.recognize: Recognition: you see the Hungarian word and recall what it means.
directionHint.produce: Production: you see the meaning and type the Hungarian word in its dictionary form.
directionHint.listen: Listening: you hear the word and recall what it means.
directionHint.cloze: Form in a sentence: you supply the missing word in the right form. These are the only cards that grade grammatical features.
directionHint.spell: Spelling: you type the word with every long vowel and umlaut.

review.scopeHint: Plan is the words from the course units. Texts is what you added yourself while reading. The daily new-card limit is one budget across both — it guards your total load, not each pile separately.
review.scopeEmpty: This pile is empty today. There is something waiting in the other one.
review.produceDictionaryForm: The dictionary form is wanted — the one a dictionary lists, not the one in the sentence. The form inside a sentence is what the “form in a sentence” card asks for.
review.practiceHint: Free practice: random words, any time. It does not affect the schedule.
review.practiceNotice: Practice. Answers here do not move the schedule and bring no word closer to “known” — this is extra practice, not review. Minutes and accuracy are counted.
review.practiceRoundDoneBody: Take another — the words do not run out. It still does not affect the schedule.
review.practiceEmpty: This pile has no words yet. Add some from the Plan or while reading.
review.practiceStatHint: Random practice outside the schedule: it does not change when a word comes back.
review.allDoneForNowBody: Everything answerable right now is answered. A few cards return later today — those are the short learning steps, by design.
review.dueSoonAuto: The queue refreshes itself when the time comes.
review.buriedToday: Held until tomorrow: {n} — other directions of words already answered today. Repeating them now would test nothing: the answer is still in memory.
review.newDeferred: New words held until tomorrow: {n} — their other direction was already in play today.

summary.missedBody: Read them over now — the scheduler asks again when their step comes round.
summary.missedBodyPractice: Practice schedules nothing: these words return to review on their own schedule.

review.practiceWeakHint: Leads with the words you are least likely to recall — judged by the same memory model that builds the schedule. The schedule itself does not move.
review.practiceWeakFallback: nothing to rank yet — this round is random

start.subtitle: What to take now: a pile on its schedule, or a practice round.
start.emptyBody: Everything scheduled for today has been answered. Practice below is always open — it schedules nothing.
start.elsewhere: In the other piles: {due} due, {new} new.

order.label: order:
order.hint: Overdue first serves the cards decaying fastest. Shuffled is a fixed random order for the day — a reload does not reshuffle it.

review.setSizeHint: The day's queue is dealt in sets of this many cards. Nothing about the schedule changes — only how big a bite you take.

set.label: set {n} of {of}
set.doneBody: Take a breath. The next set starts when you are ready — the queue is not going anywhere.
set.missedTitle: Missed in this set — read them over
set.missedBody: Each card returns when its learning step comes round: in one of the next sets, or later today. Nothing asks it early.
set.maturedList: Settled in this set (an interval of 21 days or more): {words}
set.maturedHint: “Settled” is Anki's word for a card whose next review is three weeks or more away. A convention, not a memory threshold — but a measured one.

memory.title: This card's memory
memory.graduatesNext: one more right answer and this moves to days
memory.graduatesNow: this answer moves it onto day-scale intervals
memory.stillStep: still a learning step, not the real interval yet
memory.onDays: already on day-scale intervals — from here they only grow

stageHint.new: You have never answered this card.
stageHint.learning: In its first day: short steps, minutes apart, until it moves to days. Good is the next step; Easy goes straight to days.
stageHint.young: Learned on its first day and now settling: coming back within three weeks.
stageHint.mature: Settled: coming back after three weeks or more.
stageHint.relearning: Forgotten and being relearned in short steps.

memory.word: the word, all directions: {right} of {total} right
memory.previewHint: What each grade would schedule, from the same memory model. In the learning steps Good is the next step, minutes away; Easy graduates straight to days. Approximate: the exact day is decided when you answer.

help.title: What it takes for a word to stop coming back
help.ladder: The bar above is where this word stands: new → short minute-scale steps (usually two: 1 and 10 minutes) → day-scale intervals → 21 days or more. The last segment is not a finish line — the interval just keeps growing. The bar can move back, too: a miss returns the card to the bottom of the steps.
help.next: A right answer takes the card out of today's queue: it comes back in about {good}. A miss brings it back today, in about {again}, and shortens the interval after that. The figures are approximate: the exact day is decided when you answer.
help.nextUnscheduled: This is free practice: it schedules nothing and does not move any interval. Only answers under Review change the schedule.
help.never: A card never disappears — it comes back ever more rarely: minutes, days, weeks, months, years. That is what "learned" means here; there is no end after which the word is gone.
help.notScore: "{right} of {total} right" is the log of your answers to this card, not points: nothing accumulates towards anything and nothing is lost. The memory model works the next interval out from the whole history, and there is no "N in a row" threshold.
help.notScoreUnseen: The tally that appears here after your first answer is a log, not points: nothing accumulates towards anything and nothing is lost. The memory model works the next interval out from the whole history, and there is no "N in a row" threshold.
help.know: Already know the word and see no reason to keep reviewing it? «Know it» (key t) takes the whole word out of the queue, in every direction, and marks it known. Not a delete: the cards, their state and their history all stay, and you can put it back.

know.hint: You already know this word: take it out of review and mark it known. Not a delete — you can put it back at any time.
know.done: «{word}» — marked known and taken out of the queue.
know.restored: «{word}» is back in the deck. It will not reappear in this session — it comes in the next one.

diff.vowelLength: Vowel length. It distinguishes words in Hungarian: the form is “{expected}”. This is an ear problem before it is a writing problem — worth training perception.
diff.vowelQuality: Vowel rounding. The form is “{expected}”. The front rounded vowels (ö, ő, ü, ű) have no English counterpart, so ear training is what helps here.
diff.harmony: Right case, wrong variant of the suffix: it should be “{expected}”. This is vowel harmony — a motor skill rather than knowledge, so it needs volume.
diff.feature: Wrong grammatical feature. The form is “{expected}”.
diff.stem: Different word. It should have been “{expected}”.

reader.thresholdCaveat: The {minimal} and {unassisted} marks (“readable with help” and “comfortable”) were derived on English material. Nobody has checked them for Hungarian, so treat them as a reference point, not a grade.
reader.pickAWord: Pick a word in the text.
reader.autoSpeakHint: Speak each word as you step onto it. Your device does the speaking, so this works with nothing deployed.

certainty.uncertain: This form has several readings; the more frequent one was chosen. Check it against the sense.
certainty.derived: Worked out automatically rather than looked up — it may be wrong.

reader.reportedWrong: reported as wrong — tap to retract
reader.coverageExplainWords: The first figure is the share of this text’s words you have already marked as known or taken into your cards. It counts every word as it occurs, not distinct words: a frequent word moves it once for each time it appears.
reader.coverageExplainGrammar: The second is stricter. A word counts only if you know both the word itself and every grammatical feature on it. You can know “ház” and still be stopped by “házaimban”.
reader.coverageExplainRaise: The second figure is raised by grammar drills and cloze cards — they are the only ones that grade features. Plain reading and recognition cards do not move it. It can also fall on its own: a feature you have not practised for a while stops counting as learned.
reader.noLemmaForStatus: This word is not in the language pack, so there is nothing to attach a knowledge state to yet. You can still make a card from it.
reader.ownGlossHint: Kept in your dictionary, and goes on the back of the card.
reader.machineNotOnCards: This will not go on a card: the back of a card is what you are graded against, and nobody has read this line. Accept it as yours and it becomes part of the card.

translation.fallback: (in Russian — the pack has no English translation)
translation.notConfigured: No translator is set up. Settings → Services → Translation.
translation.unreachable: The translator is not answering. It may still be loading its model.
translation.machine: Machine translation, {model}. Nobody has checked this line — use it as a crib, not as the answer.

library.title: Title
library.titleHint: optional — we take the opening words
library.textHint: Paste an article, subtitles or a chat log — something you actually wanted to read.
library.empty: Nothing here yet. Paste something you genuinely want to read — difficulty is handled by selecting sentences, not by simplifying the text.
library.subtitle: Read what genuinely interests you — words from your texts become cards.
library.noWordsYet: No deck words yet — add them while reading.
library.nothingFoundBody: No text matches the current search and filters.

gate.notEnoughYet: not enough answers to judge yet
gate.whyTitle: Why topics are not mixed from the start
gate.whyBody: Mixing topics together — interleaving — is genuinely useful, but not from the first lesson. The evidence says its benefit is much smaller for explicit grammar rules than the popular advice implies, and that before you have a working grasp of a rule the extra load actually prevents you from forming it. So the app practises one thing at a time until you are reliably right, and only then starts mixing in contrasting forms.
gate.whyNumbers: Here: blocked practice until {gate}% accuracy over the last {window} answers, then interleaved. Mastery needs {mastery}% over {masteryWindow} interleaved answers. A topic drops back if accuracy falls more than {hysteresis} points below the gate — the door swings both ways.
gate.whyCaveat: The thresholds come from studies whose participants were not you, which is exactly why they are settings rather than rules. Raise or lower them in Settings.

locked.listening: Word order and focus cannot be learned from rules — they need volume of heard Hungarian first. You have {heard} h of the {need} h this topic needs.
locked.checkpoint: This level is closed by a failed checkpoint. Repair below the line, then retake it — advancing past a failed assessment is how plateaus are built.

blocked.warmup: Practising one topic at a time. {answered} of {need} answers so far — not enough to judge yet.
blocked.accuracy: Practising one topic at a time until accuracy reaches {gate}%. You are at {accuracy}%.
blocked.fallback: Back to one topic at a time: accuracy fell to {accuracy}%, below the {floor}% floor. The gate opens again at {gate}%.

interleaved.cleared: Accuracy reached {accuracy}%, past the {gate}% gate. Contrasting forms are now mixed in.
interleaved.warmup: Mixing in contrasting forms. {answered} of {need} answers towards mastery.
interleaved.accuracy: Mixed practice. Mastery needs {mastery}%; you are at {accuracy}%.
interleaved.speed: Right {accuracy}% of the time, but your median is {median} ms against a {budget} ms target. Vowel harmony is a motor skill — it counts as learned when it is fast, not merely correct.
interleaved.lost: Accuracy slipped to {accuracy}%, below the {mastery}% mastery bar. Back to mixed practice.

mastered.reached: Mastered at {accuracy}% under mixed practice. It will keep coming back for maintenance.
mastered.automated: Automated: median {median} ms, inside the {budget} ms target. Speed is the point for a motor skill.

explained.ruleCardOnly: This topic is taught by its explanation. We have not built exercises for it, so it does not hold up anything after it.

advice.prereq: The course order suggests “{topic}” first — advice, not a lock: this topic is open now.

grammar.title: Grammar
grammar.ruleStillApplies: The explanation above is still the lesson — read it, then move on.

lesson.invariant: one variant — nothing to choose between
lesson.harmonyNote: Which variant a word takes is decided by the vowels of its stem: that is vowel harmony. The rule lands immediately and takes months to automate, which is why the exercises measure speed as well as accuracy.
lesson.startDrillsHint: The explanation stays right here — scroll back up to it whenever you want.
lesson.title: Explanation

placement.title: Placement
placement.intro: A short ladder up the curriculum, three items per topic, so you do not have to start at the alphabet. It stops as soon as two topics in a row go badly.
placement.done: Here is what the test decided
placement.honesty: Nothing is marked mastered: three items cannot show that. Each topic is seeded with exactly the answers you gave, so the scheduler knows how little it has to go on and keeps measuring.

grammar.keysTyped: Enter — check · Enter again — next item

prompt.cloze: Put {lemma} into the form the sentence needs ({feature}).

unavailable.noGenerator: We have not built exercises for this topic yet. Its explanation is real; the drills are not there.
unavailable.noPack: No language pack is installed, so no exercises can be generated.
unavailable.noMaterial: The language pack has no real examples for this topic, and we will not invent answers.

remedy.volume: understood but not yet automatic — it needs repetition, measured in speed
remedy.rule: the rule itself is not holding — read it again, then drill it
remedy.ear: this is a hearing problem wearing a spelling costume. Vowel length and rounding are not distinguishable to a Russian or English ear without training, and no amount of typing fixes that — it needs the ear trainer.
remedy.vocabulary: a different word entirely — that is the review deck's job, not grammar

ear.title: Ear
ear.refusedTitle: Not enough voices for honest training
ear.refusedBody: This pack has {have} distinct voices; high-variability training needs {need}. The variety of talkers is the ingredient that makes the training transfer to real speech — with too few voices you learn the voices, not the sounds.
ear.refusedHint: An admin can lower the bar in settings (hvpt.minTalkers). That trades away some of the effect and the app will not pretend otherwise. All available voices here are synthetic — a stated limitation of this pack.
ear.neverDone: No contrast is ever finished: perception gains decay, so every contrast keeps coming back on its own schedule. That is by design.
ear.autoplayBlocked: The browser refused to play audio without a click. Press the sound button above — and do not answer blind: a guess against silence poisons the contrast statistics.

intro.title: Ear trainer
intro.what: You hear one word from a pair that sounds nearly identical, and choose which one it was. `tör` and `tőr`, for instance, differ only in vowel length — obvious in writing, not at all obvious by ear at first. The point is to learn to hear the difference rather than infer it from meaning.
intro.why: The same word arrives in different voices, and not for variety's sake: it is the change of talker that carries the skill over to real speech. Train on one voice and you learn to understand that voice, not the language.
intro.voices: This language pack has three synthetic voices. The research asks for five or more real ones — so some of the effect is lost here, and the app does not pretend otherwise. The audio is synthesised: individual words may sound unnatural.

listen.title: Listen
listen.whyTranscript: The text is required: passes 2–3 and the comprehensibility check are built on it. It goes through the same analysis as a reading text.
listen.empty: No materials yet. Paste any Hungarian text and your device's voice will read it. An audio file is welcome but not required.
listen.coverageWarn: Element coverage is {pct}% — below ~90% this is decoding, not listening practice. Consider an easier text first; the thresholds are English-derived and indicative only.
listen.pass1Hint: First pass: no transcript. Listen for what it is about — the transcript appears in pass 2.
listen.audioOptional: An audio file, if you have one. Without it your device's own voice reads the text.
listen.deviceVoiceCaveat: This is your system's speech synthesiser, not a person. The intonation is flatter and vowel length comes through less clearly than from a speaker. Good enough for passes 1–2 and for dictation; not a substitute for a real recording.

intro.title: How this works
intro.what: Listening is not «play it once and understand everything». The same material is worked through three times, and each pass has a different job.
intro.passes: 1) Audio only, no text: get used to the pace and to where words end. 2) Audio with the transcript: check what you heard against what was said. 3) Sentence dictation: confirm it was hearing and not guesswork.
intro.caveat: With no recording, your device's own voice reads the text — the quality depends on the voices installed on your system, and individual words may sound unnatural. A transcript is required: the coverage check and passes 2 and 3 are all built on it.

progress.title: Progress
progress.noLemmas: No lemmas in play yet — start with reading or with the review deck.
progress.targetsCaveat: The A1–B2 lines are the source plan's month-milestone targets. They are reference points, not judgements, and the CEFR mapping is approximate.
progress.noMastery: Nothing graded yet. Cloze reviews and grammar drills feed this map.
progress.heatmapLead: The share of correct answers for each kind of grammar. A figure appears once there are enough answers to trust it.
progress.locativeLead: Nine cells: “inside / on / beside” × “where / whither / whence”. Colour is the share of correct answers.
progress.locativeLegend: Grey means you have not met this form yet.
progress.nothingMeasuredYet: No feature has enough answers behind it yet, so none of these figures is worth trusting. That is normal early on.

chart.title: Activity by day
chart.empty: Nothing to show yet — the data appears as soon as you start working.
chart.alt: Bar chart: minutes of study per day over {n} days, split by kind. There is an «As a table» button beside it with the same numbers as text.
chart.unmetQueue: goal not met — {n} still in the queue
chart.unmetBoth: goal not met — {done} of {goal} min, and {n} still in the queue

checkpoint.title: Checkpoints
checkpoint.failed: Failed — and that blocks advancing, on purpose.
checkpoint.rollback: The rule from the source plan: a failed checkpoint stops the programme until you find what broke. The findings above are what the data supports.
checkpoint.selfAttested: your own word — the app cannot verify this

m3.monologue: A teacher understood my recorded 5-minute monologue without asking me to repeat

diag.missedDays: Missed days: {n} of the last 30 did not meet the obligations. This is the most common cause of failure.
diag.inputTooHard: Input too hard: average element coverage of what you read was {pct}% — below the ~90% floor, reading is decoding.
diag.noLivePractice: No live practice attested in 30 days. The app cannot do this loop for you — that is exactly why it is on the Today screen.

speech.off: Speech is switched off — turn it on in Settings
speech.noVoice: This device has no Hungarian voice
speech.noVoiceHint: No Hungarian voice is installed on this device, so there is nothing to speak with. On macOS add one under Accessibility → Spoken Content → System Voice → Manage Voices; on Windows under Time & Language → Speech.
speech.unsupportedHint: This browser does not support speech synthesis, so there will be no audio here.
speech.title: Speech
speech.hint: Hungarian is spoken by your own device — the server is not involved and there is nothing to configure. Quality depends on the voices installed on your system.
speech.compactHint: Sounds robotic? That is the built-in “compact” voice — your system has a better one, it just needs downloading. macOS: Accessibility → Spoken Content → System Voice → Manage Voices, and pick the Hungarian entry marked Enhanced or Premium. Windows: Time & Language → Speech → Manage voices. It appears in the list above once installed. While the voice is a compact one the app reads slightly slower, which makes vowel length easier to hear.

inspector.thisForm: what this form is made of
inspector.noExamples: The language pack has no sentence using this word, and we will not invent one.

ai.caveat: The entry will be written by {model}. It is not a dictionary: check it. Nothing reaches a card on its own.
ai.unknown: {model} does not know this word either. An honest dead end — but not an invented entry.
ai.examplesCaveat: These are the model's examples, not real ones from the pack: they are unchecked against the corpus and never become cards.
ai.savedHint: Saved as a machine meaning. To put it on a card's back, accept it as your own in the dictionary.
ai.chipExamples: Give me three more examples with «{word}»

words.title: Words
words.subtitle: The whole deck as a list: what holds, what wobbles, what comes up next.
words.emptyBody: Words appear when you take a course unit into work or add them while reading.

tutor.title: Ask the tutor
tutor.lead: A question about this rule — in your language. The tutor answers from the lesson above, the pack's own feature tables and a reference corpus of open grammars. This chat is pinned to this topic; the AI Teacher page takes any question.
tutor.off: No language model is configured, so there is no tutor here yet. Point Settings → Services → Language model at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — a local Ollama will do — and this panel comes alive.
tutor.notice: The explanation is the model's; the lesson above is the app's. Nothing said here becomes a card, a meaning or a grade — words come from the reader and the course.
tutor.unattested: Not found in the dictionary: {words}. The model may have invented these — check before you trust them.
tutor.interrupted: The answer was cut off here.
tutor.editing: Editing a question: the old answer and everything after it will be removed.

context.known: Model window {window} tokens: the last question and answer took {used}, about {free} free.
context.unknown: Last question: {prompt} prompt tokens, answer {answer}. The model does not report its window.
context.full: The model's window is full ({window} tokens): the head of the prompt may have been cut, so the model did not see the rules and the lesson. Raise the context in Ollama to 8k.
context.none: The model reported no usage for the last answer — the previous figures are not shown in its place.

cut.budget: The answer was cut off: it ran out of the length it was allowed.
cut.timeout: The answer was cut off: the model ran out of the time it was allowed.
cut.connection: The answer was cut off: the connection to the model was lost.
cut.echo: The answer was cut: the model began repeating the prompt's own scaffolding.

tutor.smallModel: {model} is a small model: {size} billion parameters, going by its name. Models this size are often wrong about Hungarian — check its translations and breakdowns. The tutor was built for 7–8 billion, qwen3:8b for example.
tutor.sources: Reference material: the pack's lesson, the pack's feature tables, and open grammars — {sources}.

suggest.russian: How does this compare with Russian?

pin.label: Topic of the new chat

known.title: Known
known.subtitle: Words you have marked as already known. Nothing is deleted — you can put any of them back into review.
known.notice: A marked word leaves review: no intervals run, the queue does not show it and it is in no counter. Nothing is deleted — the card and its whole history are still here, and the word itself is marked known, so the reader stops highlighting it as unfamiliar. You can still practise these words, and it changes no schedule.
known.restoreHint: Put this word back into review ({n} cards)
known.emptyBody: Met a word you already know? Review has a «Know it» button — the word leaves the queue and is marked known, and you will find it here.
